title: The Prompt Is Still a Punch Card - Ted Johnson, JoinIn AI
talk_summary: He demos conversational interfaces (Nvidia Persona Plex, JoinIn AI) where the system tracks speakers, labels utterances, and chooses its own turn, and urges designers to move burden off humans.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of accepting a fully packaged request and running it, the system is allowed to ask a follow-up or confirm scope mid-task before committing, e.g. 'Want me to update the requirement to a 10,000 threshold?'
takeaways.evidence_quote: It can ask a follow-up. It can clarify mid-thought. It can notice it's missing something and say so.

takeaways.technique: Ambient capture of decisions into requirements
takeaways.what_they_do: The AI listens to the working conversation, labels statements as question/proposal/answer, and on request writes the resolved scope into a structured requirement, including later amendments.
takeaways.evidence_quote: First release supports expense approvals only. Access requests are out of scope.

takeaways.technique: Stop treating prompt incantations as the skill
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues prompt-engineering tricks (step-by-step, persona, paste more/less context) are just rules for packaging batch jobs, and the durable fix is protocol/interface design rather than magic words.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Strip the label off and it's a set of rules for packaging up good old batch.

takeaways.what_they_do: The system tags each participant's statement by type (question, proposal, answer) and by who is speaking, so it can decide what is addressed to it and when to act.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it labels each of the participants' statements as a question, a proposal, an answer, and then only takes a turn
